# p0_ai_gateway_server (Resource)

Registers an MCP server behind an AI gateway, giving agents access to your resources.

To reference an AWS- or GCP-federated credential, install the corresponding `p0_aws_oidc_identity` or
`p0_gcp_wif_identity` resource first and pass its `id` as `credential.provider`.

For the full install steps, see [MCP server](https://docs.p0.dev/integrations/resource-integrations/agentic-gateway/mcp-server).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# See the p0_ai_gateway example for the full staged-install pattern.
resource "p0_ai_gateway_staged" "example" {
  id = "primary"
  domain_hosting = {
    url            = "https://gateway.example.com"
    oauth_endpoint = "https://oauth.gateway.example.com"
  }
  lets_encrypt_email = "admin@example.com"
  oidc_client_id     = "your-upstream-oidc-client-id"
  storage_class      = "gp2"
}

# Uses the p0-security/p0-ai-gateway-stack/kubernetes module:
# https://github.com/p0-security/terraform-kubernetes-p0-ai-gateway-stack
module "ai_gateway_stack" {
  source  = "p0-security/p0-ai-gateway-stack/kubernetes"
  version = "0.3.0"

  values = [
    yamlencode({
      "agentic-gateway" = {
        agenticGatewayServer = {
          manageAllowedEmails = p0_ai_gateway_staged.example.service_account_email
        }
      }
    }),
  ]
}

resource "p0_ai_gateway" "example" {
  id = p0_ai_gateway_staged.example.id
  domain_hosting = {
    load_balancer_ip = "<your-gateway-loadbalancer-ip>"
  }
  depends_on = [module.ai_gateway_stack]
}

resource "p0_identity_provider" "example" {
  id                   = "github-actions"
  issuer               = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
  dynamic_registration = true
}

# See the p0_aws_oidc_identity example for the full staged-install pattern
# (creating the AWS-side OIDC provider and role). Requires the
# p0_aws_iam_write integration to already be installed for the same account.
resource "p0_aws_oidc_identity_staged" "example" {
  id                = "github-actions"
  account_id        = "123456789012"
  oidc_provider_url = p0_identity_provider.example.issuer
  audience          = "https://github.com/my-org"
}

resource "p0_aws_oidc_identity" "example" {
  id                = p0_aws_oidc_identity_staged.example.id
  account_id        = p0_aws_oidc_identity_staged.example.account_id
  oidc_provider_url = p0_aws_oidc_identity_staged.example.oidc_provider_url
  audience          = p0_aws_oidc_identity_staged.example.audience
}

# An MCP server that federates AWS credentials via the identity above.
resource "p0_ai_gateway_server" "aws_example" {
  id      = "aws-tools"
  gateway = p0_ai_gateway.example.id
  credential = {
    type     = "aws"
    provider = p0_aws_oidc_identity.example.id
  }
  definition = {
    type = "p0"
    id   = "aws"
  }
}

# A custom, externally hosted MCP server that authenticates end users via OAuth.
resource "p0_ai_gateway_server" "custom_example" {
  id      = "custom-tools"
  gateway = p0_ai_gateway.example.id
  credential = {
    type = "oauth"
    grant = {
      type = "authorization_code"
    }
  }
  definition = {
    type = "custom"
    hosting = {
      type  = "external"
      url   = "https://tools.example.com/mcp"
      label = "Example tools"
    }
    prompt = "Use these tools to look up example data."
  }
}

# A predefined server whose credential P0 stores in a secret manager. Install the
# matching integration (here p0_github_ai) first. Each grant names the secret.
resource "p0_ai_gateway_server" "github_example" {
  id         = "github"
  gateway    = p0_ai_gateway.example.id
  credential = { type = "vault" }
  definition = {
    type = "p0"
    id   = "github"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `credential` (Attributes) The MCP server's credential source:
    - 'aws': federate credentials from an installed AWS OIDC identity
    - 'gcp': federate credentials from an installed GCP WIF identity
    - 'native': the upstream server accepts the gateway's OAuth tokens
    - 'oauth': authenticate end users via an OAuth session
    - 'vault': P0 stores the credential in a secret manager, and each grant names the secret. The predefined
      PagerDuty ('pagerdutyUs', 'pagerdutyEu'), Datadog ('datadogUs1', 'datadogUs3', 'datadogUs5', 'datadogEu1',
      'datadogAp1', 'datadogAp2', 'datadogUs1Fed') and GitHub ('github') servers use this type
    - 'generic': the gateway exchanges its own token (RFC 8693) at the token endpoint the server definition names
    - 'impersonation': P0 provisions an identity for each grant, and the gateway acts as it. The predefined
      Google Drive ('googleDrive') server uses this type (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--credential))
- `definition` (Attributes) Whether this server is predefined by P0, or a custom server definition. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--definition))
- `gateway` (String) The `id` of the `p0_ai_gateway` that hosts this server
- `id` (String) A unique identifier for this MCP server

<a id="nestedatt--credential"></a>
### Nested Schema for `credential`

Required:

- `type` (String) One of 'aws', 'gcp', 'native', 'oauth', 'vault', 'generic', or 'impersonation'.

Optional:

- `claims` (String) May only be used if 'type' is 'native'. Claims JSON. Use Liquid syntax to template request
parameters, for example `{ "scopes": {{ request.permission.role | json }} }`.
- `grant` (Attributes) Required, and may only be used, if 'type' is 'oauth'. The OAuth grant used to obtain the credential. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--credential--grant))
- `provider` (String) Required, and may only be used, if 'type' is 'aws' or 'gcp'. The `id` of the installed
federation-provider identity (a `p0_aws_oidc_identity` or `p0_gcp_wif_identity` resource).

<a id="nestedatt--credential--grant"></a>
### Nested Schema for `credential.grant`

Required:

- `type` (String) The OAuth grant type. Only 'authorization_code' is supported.

Optional:

- `scope` (String) A comma-delimited list of scopes to request.



<a id="nestedatt--definition"></a>
### Nested Schema for `definition`

Required:

- `type` (String) One of 'p0' or 'custom'.

Optional:

- `hosting` (Attributes) Required, and may only be used, if 'type' is 'custom'. Whether this server proxies to an
externally hosted server ('external') or hosts a containerized server ('container'). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--definition--hosting))
- `id` (String) Required, and may only be used, if 'type' is 'p0'. Pre-defined server identifier.
- `logo_url` (String) May only be used if 'type' is 'custom'. An address of a logo image for the server.
- `prompt` (String) Required, and may only be used, if 'type' is 'custom'. Text used to describe this server to agents.

<a id="nestedatt--definition--hosting"></a>
### Nested Schema for `definition.hosting`

Required:

- `type` (String) One of 'container' or 'external'.

Optional:

- `entrypoint` (String) Required, and may only be used, if 'type' is 'container'. Container run entrypoint; use jinja2 syntax to template request parameters and credentials.
- `image` (String) Required, and may only be used, if 'type' is 'container'. Image that hosts the MCP server.
- `label` (String) Required, and may only be used, if 'type' is 'external'. Human-friendly label for this server.
- `url` (String) Required, and may only be used, if 'type' is 'external'. URL of the externally hosted MCP server.
